title: The three-year JUSTIS project and the budgets that outlasted it

beats.text: San Francisco expected its justice system upgrade to take three years.

visual.sub: A three-year estimate grew as the project took on more work

beats.text: The original high estimate was $15 million. Then the scope grew.

visual.label: A three-year estimate grew as the project took on more work

beats.text: A decade in, the auditor counted nearly $16.8 million in spending.

visual.kicker: Ten years in, the audit identified both spending and spending authority

beats.text: The much quoted $25.5 million was spending authority.
The grand jury disclosed a conflicting $23 million development estimate in an endnote.

visual.kicker: The grand jury flagged a second figure it could not reconcile

beats.text: The public ledger reveals why simply adding the figures fails.

visual.kicker: The City Administrator’s ledger contains a $19.19 million offset

beats.text: One department’s account contains about $19.19 million in transfer adjustments.
A later nine-year budget covered a different stretch of the program.

visual.kicker: A later budget covered an operating system and its modernization

beats.text: By 2025, the city’s technology chief said the original council had fulfilled its mandate.

visual.kicker: A later budget covered an operating system and its modernization

beats.text: A later modernization report separated funding spent from the balance carried forward.
